faq.q: How long should I leave the mehndi paste on?
faq.a: Keep the paste on for at least four to six hours. Many people leave it overnight for a darker stain.

faq.q: Why does my mehndi look orange at first?
faq.a: Fresh henna stains are orange. The colour deepens to reddish brown over the next 24 to 48 hours as the dye oxidises.

faq.q: Is black henna safe?
faq.a: Natural henna is never black. Products sold as black henna often contain PPD, a hair-dye chemical that can cause skin reactions, so they are best avoided.

title: Ornate Modern Peacock Motif Mehndi Design for Arm
descriptionParagraphs: A sophisticated modern mehndi design tailored for the arm, featuring leaf trail and heart vine. Rated as Hard, this pattern is perfect for Teej.

Henna on the forearm stains lighter than on the palm because the skin is thinner. Arm designs are easier to apply on someone else than on yourself, especially past the wrist. This pattern needs steady pressure control and fine line work, so it is best attempted after practising simpler designs.

The darker the bridal mehndi stain, the more it traditionally symbolizes a loving and supportive mother-in-law. Modern bridal mehndi has evolved to include portraits, venue sketches, and love story panels.
Application tips: Avoid water on the mehndi for at least 12 hours after paste removal. Eucalyptus oil or Vicks VapoRub applied before the design can enhance the stain.

image.alt: Modern Peacock Motif mehndi design for arm — ornate henna pattern

faq.q: How long does bridal mehndi take?
faq.a: Full bridal mehndi (both hands and feet) typically takes 4-8 hours depending on design complexity.

faq.q: How can I make my bridal mehndi darker?
faq.a: Leave paste on overnight, apply lemon-sugar sealant, keep hands warm, and avoid water for 12-24 hours after removal.

faq.q: Should the groom get mehndi too?
faq.a: In many South Asian traditions, the groom gets minimal mehndi — often just the initials of the bride on the palm.
